strings.comment: `end` includes `$` because a double-quoted string cannot span lines in Ziman -- the lexer refuses one with `unterminated string literal`, and `"""` is the multi-line form. Without it a single stray quote put every following line of the file inside this scope, which is how one bad attribute (see `attributes`) coloured a whole file as a string.
strings.name: string.quoted.double.ziman

attributes.comment: #[derive(Json, Ord, ...)] and the module-level #![experimental] / #![deprecated("...")]. The `!` is optional: without it this rule did not match the module form at all, so the `!` coloured as logical-not and the attribute name was left bare (docs/reviews/tasks.md F75). A begin/end pair rather than one `match` since 2026-10-22: the old `#!?\[[^\]]*\]` could not see past a `]` inside the attribute's own string, and `clear`'s `#[when_unmatched("... an empty one ('[]', 'Map<K, V> {}') ...")]` has one. The match ended inside `'[]'`, the rest of the line coloured as code, and its closing quote opened a string that ran to the end of the file. Including `#strings` is what fixes it: the quoted text is consumed before `end` is tried, so a `]` inside it is never seen -- leftmost-match wins in TextMate, and the opening quote comes before that `]`.
attributes.name: meta.attribute.ziman

builtin-functions.comment: builtins available without a use; a call to one is highlighted as a builtin, not an ordinary function
builtin-functions.name: support.function.builtin.ziman

field-accessors.comment: `Row::dept`, the field-accessor shorthand for `fn(r: Row) { r.dept }`. `::` rather than `.` because `Type.member` is enum-variant access; it is one token to the lexer and tight on both sides in `--fmt`, so it colours as one operator rather than as two colons. The name after it is a *field*, never a call, which is why it is a property here and not caught by `function-calls`.

declarations.comment: Captures the name at a fn/struct declaration site distinctly from an ordinary reference to it.

patterns.comment: All three visibility levels, plus `variadic`, which modifies a parameter's type (`xs: variadic int`) rather than a declaration but belongs to the same family and is a hard keyword, so unlike `internal` it cannot be miscoloured. `internal` was missing, so one of exactly three was invisible; it is a soft keyword, so `val internal = 1` miscolours it -- the same trade the grammar already accepts for `unit` (docs/reviews/tasks.md F75).
patterns.name: storage.modifier.ziman

patterns.comment: val and var are separate scopes so a theme can tell them apart. They differ by one character and that character flips mutability, which DESIGN.md's own "val/var differ by one character" entry names as a hazard and names colour as the answer; sharing one scope made that impossible. A use site still has no scope -- that needs semantic tokens (docs/reviews/tasks.md F76).
patterns.name: storage.modifier.immutable.ziman

patterns.comment: Bare fn/struct/enum fallback -- 'declarations' already handles the common case of a keyword immediately followed by a valid name.
patterns.name: storage.type.ziman

function-calls.comment: A lowercase identifier immediately before '(' -- reliable in Ziman since call syntax is always IDENT(...) or qualifier.IDENT(...), never an arbitrary expression.
function-calls.name: entity.name.function.ziman

type-names.comment: Ziman enforces PascalCase for struct/type names (a value or function name can never start uppercase), so this is a reliable syntactic signal, not a guess.
type-names.name: entity.name.type.ziman
